title.pinyin: Wǒ shì zuò chūzūchē lái de

instruction.hanzi: 读一读，说说这些词语是什么意思。
instruction.english: Read the words and phrases aloud and say what they mean.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 你好！你也是这个大学的学生吗？
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo! Nǐ yě shì zhège dàxué de xuésheng ma?
dialogue.english: Hi! Are you a student at this university too?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 是啊，我叫安娜，在这儿学习汉语。
dialogue.pinyin: Shì a, wǒ jiào Ānnà, zài zhèr xuéxí Hànyǔ.
dialogue.english: Yes, I'm Anna. I study Chinese here.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 认识你很高兴！你是什么时候来中国的？
dialogue.pinyin: Rènshi nǐ hěn gāoxìng! Nǐ shì shénme shíhou lái Zhōngguó de?
dialogue.english: Nice to meet you! When did you come to China?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ shì èr líng èr wǔ nián bā yuè lái de.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ shì yí ge rén lái de ma?
dialogue.english: Did you come on your own?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 不是，我是和我妈妈一起来的。
dialogue.pinyin: Bú shì, wǒ shì hé wǒ māma yìqǐ lái de.
dialogue.english: No, I came with my mum.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.pinyin: Wáng Míng! Nǐ zěnme zài zhèr?
dialogue.english: Wang Ming! What are you doing here?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 安娜说你今天坐飞机回北京。
dialogue.pinyin: Ānnà shuō nǐ jīntiān zuò fēijī huí Běijīng.
dialogue.english: Anna said you were flying back to Beijing today.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 太谢谢你了！你是怎么来的？
dialogue.pinyin: Tài xièxie nǐ le! Nǐ shì zěnme lái de?
dialogue.english: Thank you so much! How did you get here?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 我是坐出租车来的。我们也坐出租车回去吧。
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ shì zuò chūzūchē lái de. Wǒmen yě zuò chūzūchē huíqu ba.
dialogue.english: I came by taxi. Let's take a taxi back too.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 这个饭店的菜太好吃了！
dialogue.pinyin: Zhège fàndiàn de cài tài hǎochī le!
dialogue.english: The food at this restaurant is so good!

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.pinyin: Shì a, wǒ yě hěn xǐhuan zhèr.
dialogue.english: It is! I really like this place too.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ shì tīng shéi shuō de?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ shì tīng Liú lǎoshī shuō de.
dialogue.english: I heard about it from Professor Liu.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 下个星期我们和刘老师一起来吧！
dialogue.pinyin: Xià ge xīngqī wǒmen hé Liú lǎoshī yìqǐ lái ba!
dialogue.english: Let's come here with Professor Liu next week!

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.pinyin: Hǎo a, tā huì hěn gāoxìng.
dialogue.english: Great idea, she'll be really pleased.

title.english: The "是……的" Construction: Focusing on When, Where or How

explanation.hanzi: 说话的人已经知道一件事发生了，想说明或者问这件事是什么时候、在哪儿、怎么（坐什么）、和谁一起做的，就用"是……的"。要强调的部分放在"是"和动词中间，"的"一般放在句子最后。肯定句里"是"可以不说，否定句用"不是……的"。
explanation.english: Use 是……的 when both speakers already know that something happened in the past, and the point of the sentence is a detail about it: WHEN (什么时候), WHERE (在哪儿), HOW (坐飞机, 坐出租车) or WITH WHOM (和谁一起). Put the detail you are stressing between 是 and the verb, and 的 at the end. In positive sentences 是 can be dropped in speech (我坐飞机来的), but 的 cannot. The negative is 不是……的.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ shì zuò fēijī lái de.

examples.hanzi: 你是什么时候来中国的？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shì shénme shíhou lái Zhōngguó de?

examples.hanzi: 安娜是在大学认识王明的。

examples.english: Anna met Wang Ming at university.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bú shì yí ge rén lái de, wǒ shì hé péngyou yìqǐ lái de.
examples.english: I didn't come alone; I came with a friend.

title.english: Saying a Full Date with the Year

explanation.hanzi: 汉语说日期的顺序是从大到小：年 → 月 → 号 → 星期。说年份的时候，一个数字一个数字地读，"0"读"líng"，比如2024年读"èr líng èr sì nián"。问年份可以说"哪年"。
explanation.english: Chinese dates go from the largest unit to the smallest: year → month → day (号) → day of the week. Read the year digit by digit, with 0 said as líng: 2024年 = èr líng èr sì nián, 1998年 = yī jiǔ jiǔ bā nián. Months and days are read as normal numbers: 9月1号 = jiǔ yuè yī hào. To ask which year, use 哪年.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān shì èr líng èr liù nián shí yuè èrshíyī hào, xīngqīsān.
Èr líng èr sì nián jiǔ yuè yī hào shì xīngqītiān.
Wǒ shì èr líng èr líng nián lái Běijīng de.
Nǐ shì nǎ nián rènshi Wáng Míng de?
examples.english: Which year did you meet Wang Ming?

title.english: Review: The Four Tones and the Neutral Tone

explanation.hanzi: 汉语有四个声调和一个轻声。读下面的字和词，注意每个声调的高低变化。轻声读得又短又轻，不标声调符号。
explanation.english: Mandarin has four tones plus the neutral tone. Read each group aloud and listen for the pitch: 1st high and level, 2nd rising, 3rd low (dipping), 4th sharply falling. Neutral-tone syllables are short and light and carry no tone mark.

examples.english: 汉语 Chinese (3rd tone at the end of a word)

explanation.hanzi: 读下面的句子，注意变调：两个三声在一起时第一个读二声；"一"和"不"在第四声前面读二声，在其他声调前面"一"读四声。
explanation.english: Read these sentences aloud and apply the tone changes you have learned: a 3rd tone before another 3rd tone becomes 2nd; 不 and 一 become 2nd tone before a 4th tone; 一 becomes 4th tone before tones 1, 2 and 3.

name.english: horizontal turning to a slanted hook

singleComponentChars.etymology: The oldest form showed a person carrying a bundle of ripe grain on their back. The grain harvest came round once every cycle of seasons, so the picture came to mean "year".

singleComponentChars.meaning: to go out, to come out
singleComponentChars.etymology: Early writers drew a foot stepping up and out of a pit or doorway. Over time the foot and the opening merged into two stacked 山-like shapes, but the meaning "to go out" stayed.
The traditional form 飛 pictured a bird with its wings spread in flight. The simplified 飞 keeps just one sweeping wing stroke and two little feathers.

prompt.hanzi: 两人一组，用"是……的"互相问问题，然后向大家介绍你的同学。
prompt.english: Work in pairs: interview each other with 是……的, then introduce your partner to the group.

activities: Interview: ask your partner 你是哪年来这儿的？ 你是怎么来的？（坐飞机/坐出租车……） 你是和谁一起来的？ 你是在哪儿认识你的好朋友的？
Report back: tell the group what you learned, e.g. 他是2025年来北京的，他是坐飞机来的。
Date practice: one person writes a date with a year (e.g. 2008年8月8号), the other reads it aloud digit by digit and says which day of the week they think it is.
Group task: plan a weekend outing together — say when you'll meet, which restaurant (饭店) you'll eat at and how you'll get there (坐出租车 / 开车 / 坐车).

title.english: When a Friend Comes to Town: Pick-ups and Hosting

culture.body:
In China, a friend arriving from out of town is rarely left to find their own way. Hosts often go to the airport or railway station in person to meet them — this is called 接 (jiē, to pick someone up), as in 接机 (jiējī, meeting someone off a plane). Turning up at the arrivals gate with a smile, like Wang Ming does for Mark, is a small but meaningful sign that the friendship matters.

The next step is almost always a meal. The host will usually 请客 (qǐngkè, treat the guests) at a good restaurant and order more dishes than anyone can finish, because a full table shows generosity. Guests are urged to eat and drink more — 多吃一点儿！ (Duō chī yìdiǎnr!) — and when the bill comes, friends may playfully compete to pay. Accepting graciously and offering to treat next time is a polite way to respond.

Getting around is easier than ever. Big cities have extensive metro (地铁 dìtiě) networks, taxis (出租车 chūzūchē) and ride-hailing apps are everywhere, and high-speed trains (高铁 gāotiě) link major cities in a few hours, often making them a convenient alternative to flying. A thoughtful host will often send the visitor a message with the best route, or simply say 我开车来接你 (Wǒ kāi chē lái jiē nǐ, I'll drive over and pick you up).
